title: Throughput benchmarking harness and methodology (wip-8)
content:
Purpose:
This doc collects the recommended harness and methodology for throughput-focused benchmarking of the serving runtime. Focus is on measuring stable, repeatable tokens/sec and request/sec numbers under realistic arrival patterns while controlling for caching, batching, and model-state effects.

Scope:
- Throughput/latency tradeoffs for text generation models (decoder-only, causal).
- Hosted and Dedicated deployment modes; single-node and multi-node experiments.
- Loadgen configs, warmup procedures, measurement windows, and reproducibility metadata.

Principles (short):
- Isolation: run benchmarks on dedicated nodes (no other user traffic). Document host hardware and driver versions.
- Repeatability: every run records commit hash, model artifact id, quantization profile, and seeds for randomization where applicable.
- Determinism where possible: disable cron jobs, background syncing, and autoscalers during experiments.
- Realism: request distributions should reflect production token/sequence-length distributions or targeted workload slices.

Environment and baseline metadata to capture for each run:
- Node type(s): GPU model, CPU, memory, kernel version, docker/container runtime version.
- Driver/stack: CUDA/cuDNN/cuBLAS/Torch/XLA versions, runtime binary commit.
- Model artifact: model name, revision hash, tokenizer version, quantization profile.
- Runtime flags: batching window, max_batch_size, kv-cache policy, sequence-length caps.
- Load generator version and commit.
- Timezone/clock sync confirmation (ntp/chrony).

Warmup procedure (recommended):
1) Cold-start load: bring up the model instance(s) and allow library JIT/compilation to finish (monitor logs for "init complete").
2) KV-cache priming: for workloads with repeated prefixes, issue a small set (~100) of representative requests to populate caches. Use identical prompts used in the main run.
3) Stepped ramp: run a 5-10 minute ramp where concurrency / qps increases gradually to target. This helps collect stable kernel selection and avoids first-request penalty affecting measurement windows.
4) Steady-state verification: confirm GPU utilization, queue length, and 95th/99th latencies have stabilized for at least 2 consecutive minutes before starting measurement window.

Load generator configuration knobs (we use our internal loadgen but map to common options):
- Mode: open-loop (fixed arrival process, e.g., Poisson) vs closed-loop (client waits for response). For latency-sensitive SLAs use closed-loop; for max throughput open-loop is more realistic.
- Arrival distribution: poisson / constant / bursty (periodic spikes).
- Target qps or concurrency: specify both target and upper/lower bounds.
- Request mix: percentage distribution of sequence lengths, prompt templates, batch sizes.
- Payload sizing: vary prompt lengths and max_new_tokens.
- Retry policy: disable client-side retries during measurement window or record retries separately.
- Timing resolution: record timestamps with microsecond resolution where possible.

Example loadgen YAML snippet (text):
---
mode: open_loop
arrival: poisson
mean_qps: 1200
clients: 50
concurrency_per_client: 16
duration: 00:30:00
ramp: 00:05:00
request_mix:
  - name: short_prompt
    seq_len_in: 32
    max_new_tokens: 64
    share: 0.6
  - name: long_prompt
    seq_len_in: 256
    max_new_tokens: 512
    share: 0.4
---
(we keep the snippet as plain text in the doc; actual harness consumes YAML)

Measurement windows and statistics: 
- Warmup/ramp is excluded from the main measurement window.
- Primary window: 10-30 minutes depending on run stability. Longer windows reduce noise.
- Repetitions: run N=3 full runs (including warmup) as a minimum. For publication use N>=5 and compute mean + 95% CI.
- Report per-run: tokens/sec, requests/sec, median latency, p95, p99, error rate, GPU utilization (avg+stdev), GPU memory (max), vCPU usage, OS-level run-queue length.
- For p99/p999 tails we recommend collecting full latency histograms and reporting both absolute and delta vs baseline.

Profiling and bottleneck attribution: 
- Correlate throughput plateaus with GPU SM utilization and achieved FLOPS. If GPU utilization < 60% but CPU run-queue high, likely CPU-side batching/serialization is the bottleneck.
- Use perf/torch profiler and nvprof/nsys traces for representative requests to identify kernel hotspots.
- Track queue lengths at runtime (inference queue, batching queue, postprocessing queue).
- Measure network egress/ingress when multi-node to detect serialization/network bottlenecks.

Reproducibility metadata to include with every run (saved as flat key=value lines):
- bench_name, bench_id, run_number
- model_name, model_revision
- runtime_commit, loadgen_commit
- hardware: gpu_model,gpu_count,cpu_model,ram_gb
- config_flags (comma-separated)
- seed
- start_time, end_time
- notes (free text)

Artifacts produced by the harness (automatically archived):
- loadgen config YAML, raw event logs, parsed aggregated metrics CSV, per-run histogram JSON, GPU traces (nsys), CPU flamegraphs, system metrics (prometheus samples)
- a tarball with the above and the reproducibility metadata file

Repeatability checklist (short):
- [ ] Verify node is dedicated (no other infra tenants).
- [ ] Confirm container/runtime/git commit hashes recorded.
- [ ] Kill/disable autoscaler and background jobs.
- [ ] Run warmup and confirm steady-state before measurement window.
- [ ] Save raw logs and artifacts to artifact store with run id.

Common pitfalls and notes:
- First-request JIT/compilation variance: always exclude the first N requests from measurements and ensure warmup triggers JIT paths.
- KV cache effects: different prompt mixes can change effective throughput; explicitly document cache priming and whether cache was enabled.
- Batching artifacts: large max_batch_size can increase throughput but hurt tail latency; document batch size distributions.
- Clock skew: ensure all clients and servers are NTP-synced. Skewed clocks make histogram alignment and percentiles wrong.
- Autoscaler noise: running with autoscalers on can inject variability; prefer static cluster for experiments.

Reporting template (per experiment):
- Short summary: target, achieved tokens/sec, median lat, p95, p99, error rate.
- Environment summary: hardware and software bullets.
- Key configs: loadgen YAML (attached), runtime flags.
- Artifacts: link to tarball and linked traces.
- Notes & interpretation: explain observed bottlenecks and recommended next steps.

Open questions / TODOs: 
- Formalize statistical test for comparing two configs (A/B) under variable workloads.
- Add standardized synthetic distributions for bursty traffic patterns used by GTM customers.
- Evaluate effect of different tokenizer choices on throughput for long-context workloads.

Notes to self: keep this doc lightweight; canonical methodology should live on Confluence (see CONFLUENCE-1234) and this file should be used as the working draft for experiments.

Last edited by Samantha Lee; please add experiment snippets or counterexamples below when you run into irregularities.
